# Class 6 {.ct}

![](../graphics/REB_Logo.png){fig-alt="Reaction Engineering Basics Logo" fig-align="center" width="200"}

## Conservation of Catalyst and Charge {.cc}

Class 6 describes how the conservation of electric charge and catalytic centers impacts the generation of mechanistic rate expressions. Enzymes, homogeneous catalysts, and heterogeneous catalysts are defined.

## Learning Outcomes {.ch}

After completing Class 6 you should...

* Know 
    * the definition of an enzyme, homogeneous catalyst, heterogeneous catalyst, catalytic site, adsorption, desorption, and adsorbed species
    * the defining equations for charge conservation, enzyme conservation, homogeneous catalyst conservation, heterogeneous catalytic site conservation, and surface coverage
* Understand
    * when a mechanism involves charged reagents or a catalytic entity, a conservation equation must be used when generating a mechanistic rate expression
    * when a conservation equation is used, the full set of Bodenstein steady-state approximations is not mathematically independent, and one approximation must be eliminated
    * in a mechanism, any reagent that is charged or includes a catalytic entity should be treated like a reactive intermediate
    * easily quantifiable concentrations of reagents that are not charged and do not include catalytic entities are acceptable in mechanistic rate expressions
    * the total amount of a catalytic entity is acceptable in mechanistic rate expressions
* Be able to
    * write conservation equations for charge or catalytic entities
    * generate mechanistic rate expressions that do not include concentrations of charged reagents or reagents that include catalytic entities

## Prepare {.ch}

* Read Section 4.5 and Examples 4.8.3, 4.8.4, and 4.8.5 from Chapter 4 of REB, The Book
